brief.scope: The fixture apps batch, slice 1 (the lever, the fault kinds, the manifest shape), the skeptic pass: judge the tests on this ref against the contract in the input file (the fixture scope and the plan). The tests are landed on this ref, red first (ops/devlane/fixtures/tests/test_fixture_lever.py, test_fixture_manifests.py, test_fixture_grade.py, ops/conductor/tests/test_findings_calibration.py, and additions to test_instrument_conventions.py). Judge whether they discriminate, whether every guarantee the plan names for slice 1 is pinned, whether the probes prove red mechanically, and whether any test would pass against a wrong lever. No implementation exists yet; do not write one.

findings.claim: The sweep accepts mismatched app names and ID prefixes, paths escaping through ../../, overlapping fault/neighbour spans, and probe commands outside probes/. A wrong lever trusting this accepted manifest can execute outside the app and misgrade neighbours.
findings.reproduce: Run the in-memory validate_manifest mutant recorded in the review output; it returns [] for name=not-the-directory-name, WRONG-* ids, ../../ paths, identical fault/neighbour spans, and probe=false.

findings.claim: The composite upsert key is not discriminated: only non-key fields change, and nullable keys are inserted only once. An implementation keyed solely by fault_id, or one allowing duplicate NULL-key rows, passes while losing or duplicating calibration data.

Grading lacks duplicate-finding, multi-fault, and closed-endpoint cases. A grader counting findings rather than distinct caught faults, assigning only the first overlapped fault, or treating touching closed spans as disjoint passes with wrong rates.
findings.reproduce: python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; s=Path('ops/devlane/fixtures/tests/test_fixture_grade.py').read_text(); assert 'src/a.py:10-12, src/b.py:5-8' not in s and 'src/a.py:8-10' not in s"

findings.claim: Legacy export is compared with the same new implementation before and after calibration, determinism is checked only by repeating one insertion order, and the tracked calibration.jsonl export is untested. A consistently changed, insertion-ordered, stdout-only exporter passes.

Malformed-row coverage removes only app, exported rows do not assert harness/model, and mixed valid-then-invalid input never proves rejection-before-action. A calibrator that drops reviewer identity and commits a prefix before refusing passes.
FAULT-KINDS checks only global token presence, not per-row mappings. Swapped kind meanings with idiom and probe-shape words in an unrelated footer survive.
All 13 manifest tests fail first on the shared missing FAULT-KINDS.md assertion, so the red run proves only file absence and not any named validation property.
The ignored/untracked file is never listed in the copy list. A make implementation that copies every listed existing path without consulting git ls-files passes.
Target refusal covers only the invoking worktree, and default placement covers only absent XDG_STATE_HOME. A make implementation ignoring linked worktrees/common-dir and always using HOME passes.
The caller already supplies C locale and UTC; assertions observe inherited locale and never inspect time. A prove implementation performing no locale or time pinning passes.

prove --fixed is tested only with all probes green and with WF_AGENT present. A fixed mode requiring identity, returning zero with a remaining red probe, or replacing markers without applying valid patches survives.

Grade does not snapshot its input record, allows arbitrary extra stdout, and verifies exact IDs/claims only for some row classes. A grader mutating the record or corrupting false-positive/unmatched rows passes.

Refusal classes are substring matches rather than exact leading lowercase class: tokens, and Abort is untested. The malformed line 'not-identity garbage expected x; found y; needed z' survives the refusal helpers.
findings.reproduce: Use SimpleNamespace(returncode=2, stderr='not-identity garbage expected x; found y; needed z\n', stdout='') with _LeverFixture.assert_refusal(..., 'identity'); it returns successfully at this ref.

findings.claim: Commit checks accept arbitrary Source and Co-Authored-By values, find the expected agent name anywhere in the message, and never verify author/committer identity. Wrong attribution can pass.
No named test pins the required ruff.toml exclusion and reason, continued linting of lane tests, or the ops/README.md fixture and lever rows. Omitting all root changes passes these suites.
